STEP 5b ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK -- CLAIM CONFIRMED, with the numbers. The extracting agent reported that ENG_EMO_09 ('Penso che studiare sia noioso' / 'I think studying is boring') is stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED in the live data, and shipped its option_text reversed (resp 1 = 'Totally agree' ... 7 = 'Completely disagree') on that basis. This claim overrides the natural reading of a source and drives what ships, so it was re-checked independently against the live table (n=1065, 9 items). CONFIRMED: ENG_EMO_09 correlates POSITIVELY with all eight positively-worded affective items -- r = 0.21, 0.39, 0.24, 0.21, 0.37, 0.35, 0.38, 0.32 (against ENG_EMO_04, 05, 06, 07, 01, 08, 03, 02 respectively), with no negative correlation anywhere; a genuinely negatively-keyed item stored unrecoded would correlate negatively with all of them. Cronbach's alpha AS STORED = 0.89, versus 0.82 if ENG_EMO_09 is flipped (8 - resp); the published affective-subscale alpha in Mameli & Passini (2017) is .87, which the as-stored figure matches and the flipped figure does not. ENG_EMO_09's mean (3.5) is also the second-lowest of the nine, consistent with a boredom item scored in the agreement direction of the others. The agent's reported range (+0.205 to +0.386) reproduces. This is a property of the deposited data (the depositors pre-recoded that column), not an IRW processing defect and not an itemtext defect -- but it means resp on THIS item runs opposite to its literal wording, which is why the public_note calls it out.

STEP 5b ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK -- CLAIM CONFIRMED, with the numbers. The extracting agent reported a defect in the PAPER (not in the IRW data): Merlo et al.'s Table 1 ENG_C composite is reproduced only after dropping THREE cognitive items (ENG_COGN_04, _05, _11), while the paper's own CFA-trimming sentence names only C5 and C11. Because this is a finding about a published source that is written into a note, it was re-checked independently against the live table (n=1065, 12 items). CONFIRMED. Paper Table 1 reports M=4.229, SD=1.316, Md=4.220, skew=-0.317, kurt=-0.169. Recomputed from live IRW data: all 12 items give M=4.356, SD=1.239, Md=4.417, skew=-0.426, kurt=+0.109 (no match); dropping the paper's OWN stated pair (05, 11) gives M=4.263, SD=1.282, Md=4.300, skew=-0.353, kurt=-0.044 (still no match); dropping 04, 05 and 11 gives M=4.229, SD=1.316, Md=4.222, skew=-0.317, kurt=-0.164 -- matching the published M and SD to three decimals and skew to three decimals, with Md and kurt within rounding/estimator convention. So the composite the authors actually analysed excluded ENG_COGN_04, and the paper's trimming list omits it. This is a reporting gap in the article, NOT an IRW data defect: all 12 items are present and complete in the IRW table (per-item n=1065), and anyone rebuilding the paper's ENG_C from this table must drop 04, 05 and 11.
